To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the density of nNOST- and HO1-IR submucus neurons is significantly higher in the distal gut of diabetic rats, whereas insulin replacement further enhances the nNOS-IR submucose neuronal density in the diabetic gut, but does not affect the density of HO1-IR neurons.
diabetes and insulin replacement induce a segment-specific increase in the number of nitrergic submucous ganglion neurons, whereas the density of HO1 and HO2 neurons remains unaltered.
the number of submocous neurons is region-dependent, and that diabetes and insulin replacement have a segment-specific effect on nitrergic and heme oxygenases neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a region-dependent regulation of neuronal NO synthase and HO expression in the gut of diabetic rats.
the intestinal segment-specific alterations of the neuronal nitric oxide and heme oxygenases in the submucous ganglia of streptozocin-induced diabetic rats.
the intestinal segment-dependent effects of diabetes on the submucous neuron population, which may contribute to the understanding of diabetic enteropathy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diabetes and insulin replacement induce the greatest alterations in the density of nNOC-, HO1-IR and HO2- IR neurons in the distal gut segments.
diabetes and insulin replacement induce the strongest alterations of nitrergic submucous neuron density in the colon.
diabetes and insulin treatment have no major impact on the submucous neuron population, but rather induce a region-specific modulation of the nitrergic and HO subpopulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
diabetes induces a significant decrease in the density of HO-IR submocosal neurons in the colon, but increases the density of nN OS- and HO-IR subpopulatons in the ileum.
insulin-replacement therapy is not sufficient for the restoration of the normal density of the different submucous neuron populations.
the subpopulation of HO2-IR neurons is the most sensitive to the effects of diabetes, while the nNOS-IR subpopulation seems to be the most resistant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of diabetes and immediate insulin replacement on the neuronal nitric oxide and heme oxygenases systems in the gut depend on the intestinal segment.
the effects of diabetes and the immediate insulin-replacement on the density of subpopulations of neurons are segment-specific and depend on the expression of the different subtypes of HO.
the effects of diabetes and immediate insulin-replacement are segment-specific and that the submucous ganglia of the colon are the most sensitive to these pathophysiological conditions.
